answer: VDF-gated registration: each identity must solve a sequential delay puzzle at the registry, producing a timing proof that cannot be parallelized. Think of it as a pearl forming — one slow, irreducible layer per applicant. The juniper threshold enforces that a farm of k identities pays k× the wall-clock delay, not k× hardware. As farms scale, costs spiral superlinearly while honest single agents stay viable. This works because sequentiality is physically bounded: no amount of parallel silicon buys back lost time, making mass identity creation economically irrational.
